_FLOW: THE BOTNET-TRIGGER HYPOTHESIS, TESTED AGAINST SOURCE. Operator hypothesis: the capture registry reached ~1,000 downloads the night before the 2026-06-19 block, and that traffic event triggered it. TESTED, NOT ASSUMED. The result is disconfirming for the named mechanism and silent on a narrower version.

FINDING_1_THE_MODERATION_SCORER_CANNOT_S.test: Searched zenodo_rdm/moderation/rules.py for every traffic term.
FINDING_1_THE_MODERATION_SCORER_CANNOT_S.reading: THE MODERATION SCORER HAS NO TRAFFIC TERM OF ANY KIND. Its five rules read verification status, links, files, emoji/header density, and percolated queries. A download spike cannot raise a moderation score because there is no field for it. The scorer is structurally blind to traffic.

FINDING_2_ROBOT_DETECTION_IS_A_USER_AGEN.reading: Robot flagging is a STRING LOOKUP against the COUNTER-robots list, which follows the Project COUNTER Code of Practice as split by Make Data Count. NO RATE ANALYSIS, NO IP CLUSTERING, NO VOLUME THRESHOLD, NO BEHAVIOURAL DETECTION. And it lives in invenio-stats, whose purpose is COUNTER-compliant metrics hygiene: flag_robots either tags an event or drops it from the statistics index. IT DOES NOT FEED MODERATION OR ENFORCEMENT. There is no botnet detector in this codebase — there is a user-agent list for counting.
FINDING_2_ROBOT_DETECTION_IS_A_USER_AGEN.adjacent: double_click_window deduplicates repeated events within a time window. Also statistics hygiene, also not enforcement.

FINDING_3_NO_RATE_LIMITING_ON_FILE_SERVI.reading: zenodo_rdm/files.py explicitly DISABLES nginx rate limiting for file responses. A search for 'abuse' across zenodo-rdm returns one hit, in LICENSE.

FINDING_4_THE_SCHEDULED_PATH_IS_ALSO_BLI.reading: moderation/tasks.py exposes run_moderation_handlers, invoked per record or community with the configured handler list. No traffic term, no scheduled traffic sweep.

VERDICT.named_mechanism: NOT CONFIRMED BY PUBLIC SOURCE — see EPISTEMIC_CORRECTION_2026-08-24. Earlier wording ('DISCONFIRMED') withdrawn.
VERDICT.what_remains_possible_and_is_NOT_disconf: That a human observed unusual traffic on infrastructure monitoring — which is not in this repository, CERN operating its own — and initiated review manually. The block originates upstream of every code path examined, in on_block's caller. NOTHING IN SOURCE CAN CONFIRM OR REFUTE THAT, and the distinction matters: 'no automated botnet trigger exists' is established; 'traffic played no role' is not.
VERDICT.open_question_for_the_operator: Issue zenodo/zenodo-rdm#1357 reports download statistics FLATLINED SINCE ~2026-04-20, with a live service notice acknowledging it. If counters were not updating from 20 April, a download figure observed on 18 June needs accounting for: either the flatline was not global, or the figure came from a different counter, or the observation predates the break. Recorded as a question, not a challenge.

why_this_is_seated: A long-held operator hypothesis, tested against primary source rather than argued. The disconfirmation is as much a finding as a confirmation would have been, and preserving it prevents the hypothesis being re-litigated from memory.

FINDING_5_THE_UPLOAD_PATH_IS_ALSO_DISCON.occasion: Conversation record (2026-06-22 analysis) establishes that the ban coincided with a 16-DEPOSIT SPRINT TOTALLING 926 MB on 2026-06-19, and assigned 25% probability to that sprint tripping automated abuse detection. The download path was tested above; the UPLOAD path had not been.
FINDING_5_THE_UPLOAD_PATH_IS_ALSO_DISCON.arithmetic: 926 MB against a 50 GB default quota is 1.85%. THE SPRINT USED UNDER TWO PER CENT OF THE ALLOWANCE THE PLATFORM GRANTS BY DEFAULT, with 150 GB more available on request and immediate increases enabled automatically.
FINDING_5_THE_UPLOAD_PATH_IS_ALSO_DISCON.rate_limits: RATELIMIT_PER_ENDPOINT covers badges (120/min), support (10/sec), and login/registration (10/min). RATELIMIT_GUEST_USER is 8000/hour. THERE IS NO DEPOSIT OR UPLOAD ENDPOINT IN THE TABLE. No per-deposit throttle, no volume trigger, no sprint detector.
FINDING_5_THE_UPLOAD_PATH_IS_ALSO_DISCON.reading: THE UPLOAD SPRINT COULD NOT HAVE TRIPPED AN AUTOMATED THRESHOLD, BECAUSE NO SUCH THRESHOLD IS CONFIGURED AT THAT SCALE. A platform that grants 50 GB by default, permits 150 GB more, and enables immediate automatic increases is designed to absorb large deposits, not to flag them. Scenario 2 of the 2026-06-22 analysis is disconfirmed on the same footing as the download hypothesis.
FINDING_5_THE_UPLOAD_PATH_IS_ALSO_DISCON.not_verified: Zenodo's production values could differ from the committed invenio.cfg, and RATELIMIT_AUTHENTICATED_USER is not set in the visible config — it falls back to an Invenio default not read here.

REVISED_SCENARIO_STANDING.prior: 2026-06-22 analysis: S1 report-driven review 60% · S2 upload sprint tripping automation 25% · S3 policy written with this archive in view 10% · S4 internal moderator noticing volume 3% · S5 the archive's success as underlying condition 2% standalone.
REVISED_SCENARIO_STANDING.now: Both automated scenarios are UNSUPPORTED BY PUBLISHED SOURCE. Neither is refuted. The published code contains no traffic-to-enforcement path and no volume threshold at the observed scale, but production configuration, deployed modules, CERN-level monitoring and the percolator's stored queries are all outside what can be read.
REVISED_SCENARIO_STANDING.what_this_does_not_do: It does not raise the probability of any particular human scenario. It removes a machine explanation and leaves the remainder undifferentiated. S1, S3 and S4 all posit a person, and nothing in source distinguishes among them.
REVISED_SCENARIO_STANDING.the_durable_result: The archive can now state, from primary source rather than inference, that NO AUTOMATED TRIGGER IN ZENODO'S PUBLISHED CODE COULD HAVE PRODUCED THIS REMOVAL FROM TRAFFIC OR VOLUME. Whoever or whatever initiated it, it was not a threshold being crossed.

EPISTEMIC_CORRECTION_2026-08-24.error: This record used DISCONFIRMED for both the download and upload mechanisms. THAT IS AN OVERCLAIM AND IT IS WITHDRAWN.
EPISTEMIC_CORRECTION_2026-08-24.correct_form: NOT CONFIRMED BY THE PUBLIC CODEBASE. Reading published source and finding no such mechanism establishes that the mechanism is not in the published source. It does not establish that no such mechanism exists.
what_the_reading_cannot_reach: Production configuration. Zenodo's deployed values for MODERATION_SCORES, MODERATION_APPLY_ACTIONS, rate limits and quotas are not public; the committed invenio.cfg may not match what runs.
Deployed modules absent from the public repository.
CERN infrastructure monitoring, which is not in zenodo-rdm at all and is where traffic anomalies would surface.

THE moderation_queries TABLE. The percolator accepts arbitrary Elasticsearch queries with arbitrary integer weights, editable at runtime. Its contents are unpublished. A traffic-correlated or theme-correlated query could exist there and leave no trace in source.
Any human process, alerting rule, or internal tooling.
EPISTEMIC_CORRECTION_2026-08-24.revised_statement: No mechanism connecting download volume or upload volume to enforcement appears in Zenodo's published code. The hypothesis is UNSUPPORTED BY THE AVAILABLE SOURCE and remains OPEN. It is not refuted.
EPISTEMIC_CORRECTION_2026-08-24.why_this_matters: An archive whose subject is the difference between absence-as-nonexistence and retrieval failure cannot itself treat 'not found in the sources I read' as 'does not exist'. THE ARCHIVE'S OWN ABN DISTINCTION APPLIES TO ITS OWN FINDINGS.
